## 固定收益市場主線

油價再度急升，借款成本重新承壓，美國公債因而吐回部分先前的強勁漲幅；投資人對人工智慧熱潮如何籌資的疑慮則未消退。10年期殖利率上升4.15個基點至4.9945%，2年及30年期升幅相近。中東暴力衝突再起，威脅原油供應，布蘭特原油收在每桶$116.72。科技股賣壓暫歇，降低了眼前的避險需求，但風險偏好並未全面回升。

美國最新經濟數據顯示，聯準會難以把消費者信心疲弱視為通膨壓力緩解。10月企業調查仍呈擴張，製造業更優於市場預期。密西根大學消費者信心雖停留在五個月低點，終值卻高於初值，短期及較長期通膨預期也雙雙上升。家庭購買力受壓、企業活動仍在成長，並非所有經濟活動同步惡化。

相較公債，信用市場的分化更明顯。美國投資級債利差明顯擴大，高收益債整體利差當日則變動不大，儘管個別低評級借款人遭遇重挫。SpaceX的晶片融資、支撐AI債務的交易架構新細節，以及Ineos Quattro債券急跌，分別凸顯資金競爭、契約支持集中，以及營運獲利不足以紓解龐大再融資負擔等問題。法國公債先行收復部分失土，美國固定收益市場收盤後不久，法國也暫時避過信評調降；不過，最新企業調查已顯示經濟陷入萎縮。

## 油價與家庭通膨預期牽制美債漲勢

週五美債各主要年期的殖利率升幅相當接近。2年期上升4.22個基點至4.6818%，5年期上升3.54個基點至4.8067%，30年期上升4.17個基點至5.3221%。2年與10年期利差僅收窄0.07個基點至31.27個基點。當日行情主要是回吐前一天的部分價格漲幅，殖利率曲線沒有明顯的新調整。

全週而言，公債仍上漲。10年與30年期殖利率分別下降7.83及9.88個基點，2年期則下降2.65個基點。但拉長至本月，10年及30年期殖利率仍分別上升3.15及2.21個基點，2年期下降7.42個基點。長天期公債一週來的反彈，尚未解除融資成本居高不下的整體負擔。

週五的反轉同時來自實質殖利率與通膨補償上升。10年期抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率上升2.98個基點至2.6415%，占名目殖利率升幅的大部分；10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1.17個基點至2.353%。全週實質殖利率下降8.05個基點，損益兩平通膨率反而微升0.22個基點。支撐美債全週表現的是實質殖利率回落，而非較長期通膨補償下降。

能源價格走勢則明顯相反。布蘭特原油週五上漲3.14%，全週與本月漲幅分別擴大至6.24%及22.34%；西德州原油上漲3.82%至$103.27，全週上漲4.29%，本月上漲17.38%。Bloomberg的市場報導將這波上漲歸因於中東暴力衝突再起及供應受威脅。不過，另一篇現貨交易報導指出，中東原油售價較低，荷姆茲海峽運輸仍在持續，顯示期貨風險溢價的上升，快於實際供應流失的證據。

股市也只是局部止穩。那斯達克100指數跌幅不到0.01%，半導體股反彈0.44%，但標普500指數下跌0.52%。晶片股全週仍下跌3.21%，本月跌幅15.05%。VIX上升2.21%至19.45，美元指數上升0.20%至101.81。科技股拋售雖暫停，整體市場仍須消化高能源價格與資金成本的不確定性。

10月S&P Global採購經理人指數初值，為推動美債上漲的成長疑慮提供了重要的當期對照。美國綜合PMI由58.4降至57.6，符合經濟日曆所列預測；服務業由58.8降至57.9，略低於共識58；製造業由55.9升至56.0，高於共識55.5。兩部門均高於榮枯分界50，製造業不僅沒有隨服務業放緩，還小幅增強。

家庭的感受卻較不樂觀。密西根大學10月消費者信心終值為48.0，高於初值及共識的46.3，但略低於9月的48.1，仍是五個月低點。訪問期間為9月22日至10月19日，反映的是高物價、招募有限及房貸利率偏高等壓力，而不只是最近交易日的消息。

疲弱主要集中在消費者對當前狀況的評價：現況指數由50.9降至46.7，預期指數則由46.3升至48.8。現況惡化完全來自耐久財購買條件，該項指標因利率升高及負擔能力疑慮下跌18%，創歷史新低。近70%受訪者預期未來一年利率上升，比例為逾三年來最高。

展望雖有改善，整體信心水準並未回升。未來一年企業景氣預期上升約14%，但仍比2025年10月低16%；整體信心比一年前低10%，比伊朗衝突前的2月低15%。共和黨與民主黨支持者的信心上升，被無黨派受訪者連續第三個月下滑所抵銷。

與此同時，通膨預期升高。未來一年通膨預期由9月的4.6%升至4.7%，未來5至10年則由3.4%升至3.5%，兩者均為5月以來最高。調查主任Joanne Hsu警告，通膨連續五年高於目標後，近期預期再度上升，凸顯通膨預期固化的風險。購買條件惡化卻伴隨預期物價漲幅提高，使政策更難回應信心疲弱。

Pimco經濟學家Tiffany Wilding認為，通膨雖高，卻未加速，因此聯準會即使要抑制AI支撐的需求，仍可採取審慎步調。這與家庭調查中通膨預期升高的訊號，著重點有所不同。無論PMI持續擴張，或密西根調查所見的負擔能力惡化，都不支持「經濟活動崩跌、物價壓力同時下降」的單一敘事。

撇開單日反轉，債券需求仍相當強。Bloomberg Intelligence估計，10月債券ETF流入約$580億，占全部ETF資金流約38%。固定收益連續第二個月取得逾35%的資金流，是去年初以來首次。BI的Athanasios Psarofagis將此歸因於配置轉趨防禦，以及利息收益具有吸引力。不過，月度資金流並未阻止週五下跌：投資級債ETF LQD當日報酬約為負0.41%，HYG約為負0.06%。

## AI融資考驗借款人，也考驗交易架構

週五藍籌企業債務的信用保險成本進一步上升。CDX投資級指數盤中一度上升1.5個基點至64.4，創3月以來盤中最高。亞洲較高評級美元公司債利差擴至2025年7月以來最寬，歐元投資級債利差也來到2025年5月以來水準。科技股即使停止下跌，融資市場的壓力仍在擴散。

Trace資料顯示，紐約時間下午4時，SpaceX票息6.6%、2046年到期債券相對美債利差擴大13個基點至279個基點。當時公司正洽談一筆$400億融資，用於購買Nvidia晶片，並試圖不把負債列入自身資產負債表。投資級評等是交易的關鍵：隨著資本需求增加，將債務分開安排的目的在於保護評等。

知情人士表示，高盛正與Apollo領頭的投資人洽談，預計由Apollo支持的Atlas SP管理融資實體，Pimco考慮參與，高盛也可能保留部分債務。擬議私募融資分三部分：$250億至$300億的次順位部分、另一筆$100億，以及最多$50億的第三部分。先前討論的利差介於基準以上230個基點至逾300個基點；次順位部分曾討論8%區間中段的殖利率，但市場波動加劇，使定價更難敲定。

先前交易已顯示，會計認定會直接影響負債歸屬。SpaceX最新財報揭露，早先一筆xAI融資中約$130億，最終因會計師將交易認定為未成立的售後租回，而列為SpaceX自身債務。該實體先前曾與Valor Equity Partners尋求籌措最多$200億。新融資面對的是一個實際先例：原本想隔離負債的架構，未能取得預期會計效果。

美國週五交易結束後，Elon Musk週日在X表示，SpaceX已完成這筆$400億晶片融資，並提到公司的投資級評等，以及Starlink與火箭發射收入。但知情人士向Bloomberg表示，週日仍在討論定價，交易尚未完成。Musk另稱，貸款機構大致已停止向缺乏AI資料中心以外大量收入的公司提供資金，並預測新型雲端業者將整併。亞洲一週交易開始時，這筆融資是否完成仍存在相互矛盾的說法。

晶片擔保融資的新報導，也說明債權人為何區分公司整體信用與個別交易風險。CoreWeave部分非投資級公司債已跌至面額約80%，殖利率約15%；其兩筆晶片擔保槓桿貸款僅小幅下跌，仍接近平價。投資人對成長中公司的債權，與由特定客戶合約及硬體支持的債權，給予不同評價。

這類架構通常由特殊目的實體持有晶片，以客戶現金流與設備作擔保借款，再以合約付款支付利息、攤還本金；到期年限多配合晶片預期五至六年的折舊期間。Bloomberg調查指出，晶片成本可達容納這些晶片的資料中心的兩至四倍。Nscale位於西維吉尼亞州的旗艦開發案，預估GPU支出$470億，資料中心及設備$180億，發電廠$65億。

硬體使用年限短，使融資需求龐大且反覆出現。摩根大通分析師估計，至2030年的晶片支出可能超過$3兆，其中大部分可能仰賴債務。供應商支持正協助這些需求接上投資級資金。Nvidia已宣布與六大貸款機構建立$5,000億合作關係，並在其8月組成的聯盟下，為單筆機會提供最多25%的支持。Broadcom則正與華爾街合作，籌組$600億融資實體，購買晶片並出租給Anthropic。

契約背後的支持不同，借款成本也相差甚遠。CoreWeave在2023年取得的首筆$23億私募信貸，由Blackstone主導、以Microsoft合約支持，利率位於十幾個百分點的中段。3月另一筆由Meta合約支持的$85億融資，借款成本約6%，反映貸款人依Meta較強的信用評估該筆交易。這兩筆融資的日期與條件不同，成本差距並不代表CoreWeave整體企業融資成本普遍下降。

Apollo與Blackstone為Anthropic安排的$350億Big Sky融資，是另一個例子。Broadcom承諾，若Anthropic違約，晶片將重新出租或出售，剩餘缺口由Broadcom補足。這項支持讓兩筆優先順位融資取得投資級評等；其中最大一筆利率5.75%，風險較高的$45億次順位部分則為8.5%。交易背後的平台可支應20吉瓦容量，美國銀行策略師估計，到2029年中可能需要$2,350億具支持承諾的債務。

這些保護也使信用依賴集中於少數晶片商與客戶。惠譽的Jason Pompeii警告，如此規模的供應商融資，會提高AI表現不如預期時衝擊沿供應鏈擴散的可能性。Carlyle的Akhil Bansal質疑，若提供信用支持的少數科技公司日後要求修改合約，實際談判力量將如何分配。Nuveen的Laura Parrott暫不大舉參與投資級晶片交易，等待市場累積更多架構在受衝擊時的運作經驗。相較之下，Apollo的Chris Edson強調抵押品、本金攤還、有限的殘值或續約風險、分散配置及高評級客戶等交易條件。

債市以外的籌資也遇到阻力。SK海力士因監管與股東反對，放棄Solidigm潛在$100億美國上市案，疑慮包括少數股東權益稀釋及持股結構複雜。Bloomberg另報導，OpenAI為約$300億募資所尋求的估值，由先前$1.4兆降至$1.25兆。Solidigm撤案有特定公司治理原因，OpenAI則直接調整了擬議股權融資條件。

日圓信用市場方面，韓國輸出入銀行（KEXIM）延後原本最快10月23日定價的發債。該行表示，波動使其無法按規劃價格達到目標規模，且沒有迫切資金需求；此前已探詢3年、5年及7年期需求。買方資金競爭相當激烈：10月截至週五，公司債定價超過¥2.5兆，創同期月份紀錄，其中樂天發行¥4,000億、瑞穗銀行¥2,810億。NTT Finance原擬籌約¥1,000億，最終僅取得¥700億，三井不動產也已擱置發債。

## 法國經濟轉弱，信評暫獲喘息

法國公債週五反彈，10年期對德國公債利差收窄7個基點，為10月6日以來最大單日收窄。不過，利差仍約1.7個百分點，全週擴大29個基點，是1990年有資料以來第二大單週升幅。單日改善紓解了眼前壓力，並未扭轉法國財政風險累積的重新定價。

新的經濟數據比預期疲弱。法國10月S&P Global綜合PMI由51.1降至48.4，低於預測50.3，製造業與服務業均跌破50。S&P Global經濟學家Joe Hayes指出，融資收緊及政治壓力伴隨採購與投資減少，民間部門銷售降速為5月以來最快；未來一年活動預期降至六年半低點。預算困局因而也有了具體的成長壓力。

紐約時間下午5時剛過，Moody’s維持法國Aa3評等、展望負向，未如投資人預期調降。該機構表示，成長放緩及赤字升高，使債務負擔超過先前預期；殖利率上升也快於預測，抗議活動則可能限制財政整頓。法國保住主要評等機構中最後一個AA級評等，比S&P及惠譽高一級。

Moody’s假設，旨在降低赤字的2027年預算最終會通過，可能透過行政命令。今年赤字預估為GDP的5.4%；總理Sebastien Lecornu擬藉支出節制與增加稅收，將明年赤字降至5%。但政府未掌握國會多數，如何落實仍不確定。國民議會週五否決社會安全預算的收入部分，原始草案轉交參議院；主要預算辯論預定下週恢復。

ECB面對的課題，是區分共同能源衝擊與個別國家的財政壓力。其消費者調查顯示，9月一年期通膨預期由8月的3%升至3.1%，三年期維持2.9%，五年期維持2.5%。上升集中於短期，並未擴及三個期限。

Bloomberg新一輪經濟學家調查也顯示，政策預測與市場定價有落差。絕大多數受訪者預期12月再升息25個基點、存款利率達2.75%後，將維持至2028年5月；交易員則預期未來一年還會升息三次。Rabobank的Bas van Geffen認為，能源尚未對更廣泛的工資及價格設定產生影響，是可以等待的理由；International School of Management講師Dennis Shen則認為，整體通膨長期超標，會提高預期與工資的中期風險。

經濟學家認為，ECB直接支持主權債的門檻很高。約70%排除任何形式的干預，約90%排除動用傳導保護工具（TPI）。Bank J Safra Sarasin的Karsten Junius表示，全球資金需求增強、公共財政惡化，讓TPI操作難以合理化。部分受訪者認為，較溫和的利率指引或停止量化緊縮較有可能；這與透過購債壓低法國借款溢價，有相當大的差別。

領導人事協商也逐漸與這項挑戰交織。歐元區部長將Isabel Schnabel執委席次的申請期限由10月28日延至11月27日，提高了將其接任人選、總裁及Philip Lane職位一併協商的可能性。調查中，12人認為Pablo Hernandez de Cos最可能出任下任總裁，九人選擇Klaas Knot。只有三分之一預期Christine Lagarde會做滿至2027年10月的任期，前次調查則近60%。

週末報導指出，各國政府評估候選人時，更重視危機處理的可信度。前ECB首席經濟學家Peter Praet強調干預條件與央行獨立性；de Cos本月演說警告，公共融資需求龐大時，即使操作設計完善，也可能被從財政角度解讀。Knot本月的論文則主張，市場分裂若威脅貨幣政策傳導，緊急工具有其正當性。爭論不只在於願不願意採取行動，也在於什麼條件下才能行動。

英國投資人對財政風險的反應有所不同。Rathbones在旗下£96億多元資產組合買進10年期英國公債、賣出2至5年期債券，將較長天期曝險由低配調至中性。David Coombs提到，預算溝通更有紀律，實質殖利率也接近2%，但仍懷疑能否節制支出。Royal London經理人Craig Inches與Ben Nicholl則已另行加碼30年期英國公債，看重財政紀律、長天期發行減少，以及英國央行量化緊縮計畫的調整。

Royal London仍對短天期英國公債保持戒心，因為通膨可能迫使英國央行繼續升息，市場已反映未來一年逾100個基點的升幅。偏好長天期債券，是基於供給與財政變化，而非認為短期通膨問題已消失。Bloomberg週五市場報導所列，英國10年期公債殖利率上升3個基點至5.36%，德國10年期則上升1個基點至3.35%。

## 日本公債大漲，通膨與政策訊號卻偏緊

日本公債大漲，即使最新通膨證據仍支持日本央行進一步緊縮。週五盤中10年期殖利率下降12.5個基點至2.755%，5年期最多下降10.5個基點至2.185%。法國巴黎資產管理的Ryutaro Kimura認為，短中天期殖利率下跌，顯示投資人正納入一種可能：若科技股跌勢與歐洲債務壓力演變為持續性金融衝擊，升息可能延後。

日本9月不含生鮮食品CPI年增2.1%，符合預測中位數，也是今年首次高於日本央行目標；不含生鮮食品及能源的指標年增2.4%，整體CPI年增2.1%。服務價格漲幅加速至1.5%，為3月以來最快。不含生鮮的食品價格上漲2.9%，即使米價下跌20.6%，創1971年以來資料最大跌幅。

除了能源，價格上漲的廣度同樣重要。旅館、水費及食品成本領漲，汽油稅調降則繼續壓抑消費者能源支出。帝國資料銀行表示，主要食品及飲料公司計畫10月調漲3,153項產品，連續第二個月超過3,000項，為2023年7月以來首見。全球避險需求壓低殖利率之際，企業轉嫁成本的意願，仍為日本央行提供國內價格訊號。

熟悉日本央行想法的人士向Bloomberg表示，官員認為基礎通膨大致符合2%，政策利率距中性水準仍有一段距離。若經濟及物價依預期發展，他們認為有空間維持近期約每季升息一次的步調，同時評估累積效果與風險，沒有預定路徑；9月才升息，也不急於立即再動。這項政策訊息與市場的防禦性買盤形成對照。

中國借款成本下降則有不同背景。財政部週五發行人民幣155億離岸國債，2年、5年及10年期標售殖利率分別為1.24%、1.38%及1.67%，均創新低；3年期為1.28%，是2011年以來最低。殖利率創低之際，整體投標倍數卻降至3.43倍，為2025年5月以來最低。

境內方面，考慮發行規模縮小後，30年期國債標售投標倍數仍創2007年有資料以來新高。中國人民銀行連續第三天淨投放資金，隔夜附買回利率約1.27%，接近數月低點。在這樣的資金環境下，境內10年期殖利率10月已下降約5個基點。

週五財政數據則說明，政府支持尚未轉化為更強支出。Bloomberg根據財政部資料計算，9月廣義財政支出年減3.7%，連續第七個月下降，但跌幅小於8月的6.7%；收入下降3.5%，單月赤字縮小3.8%。前九個月廣義支出超過收入人民幣7.57兆。

地方政府已發行人民幣3.56兆新增專項債，占全年預算計畫81%，但廣義支出僅達全年目標65%，低於一年前的67%。前九個月土地出讓收入下降27.9%，拖累土地相關支出下降18.5%。財政部表示有意加快下達明年專項債額度，以便1月開始發行。融資安排與實際資金運用的進度並不一致。

其他國家貨幣決策仍取決於各自情勢。俄羅斯維持關鍵利率14%，總裁Elvira Nabiullina表示，理事會詳細討論的選項只有維持不變。遭烏克蘭攻擊受損的工業產能恢復較慢，需要比先前預期更長時間維持適度緊縮。央行預測年底通膨7.1%至7.6%，明年平均政策利率12.5%至13.5%，2026年成長率由0%至1%修為0.5%至1%。Nabiullina表示，需要債務重整的大型企業多為暫時困難，未見金融穩定威脅。

哈薩克降息50個基點至15.75%，為連續第四次降息，此前9月通膨降至9.3%。受訪經濟學家中三人預期降50個基點，四人預期25個基點。央行表示，今年不太可能再調整，理由包括物價壓力仍高、通膨風險，以及受管制費率的基期效應可能使通膨再升。

印度的Sanjay Malhotra週五表示，某些情況下利率可用於金融穩定，但維持物價穩定仍是首要目的。他重申印度央行著眼匯市有序交易，而非盧比的特定價位。盧比本月稍早一度接近兌美元97，當日收在94.94。印度央行月報警告，食品與燃料通膨正擴散，可能產生第二輪效應；Malhotra則指出，9月5.54%的通膨仍在以4%為目標、介於2%至6%的容忍區間內。

印尼的信用重新定價，顯示股市治理問題如何延伸至債務。在MSCI提出重新分類警告後，印尼公司債相對區域同業的利差增加28個基點至67個基點，為2020年以來最寬。自10月15日宣布以來，Bank Mandiri的AT1下跌3點至面額約95%，亞洲高收益債整體僅跌0.8點；Bank Negara Indonesia同類證券連跌六次後約為94%，但兩家銀行的優先順位債均仍約99%。野村的Nicholas Yap認為，大型銀行的強健資本及資金來源可提供緩衝，但在指數決定或國內情緒更明朗前，次順位債估值料仍承壓。

## 獲利與債權條款牽動困境債務

Ineos Quattro週五公布獲利，帶來鮮明的個別發行人衝擊。第三季EBITDA由一年前€1.77億降至€1.62億，也遠低於第二季的€4.07億；第二季曾因亞洲進口受阻，暫時獲得價格支撐。2029年3月到期債券每€1面額下跌€0.09，邁向2023年11月發行以來最大單日跌幅。ICE Data Services顯示，違約保險前端費用由25.6點升至31點。

公司將疲弱歸因於低成本亞洲進口回流，以及尤其在歐洲居高不下的能源成本。Inovyn的EBITDA由一年前€6,400萬降至€1,300萬，進口干擾帶來的價格支持大致消失，電力與天然氣成本卻上升。中國供給過剩也壓縮聚合物利潤率，美國市場則相對較強。Bloomberg Intelligence的Timothy Riminton指出，2029年約有€40億債務到期。新一波獲利下滑，削弱了公司面對這筆再融資負擔的營運緩衝。

更廣泛的研究顯示，低評級尾端的困境正在加深。摩根大通指出，9月價格低於面額60%的貸款規模，為2020年3月以來最高；價格不高於80%的規模，12個月增加近90%。CCC與BB級利差差距擴至疫情以來最大。有線電視與衛星業借款人表現尤其弱，同時承受高融資成本及新傳播技術競爭。

個別借款人的集中損失是否預示全面信用下行，市場仍有不同看法。CPP Investments的David Colla警告，企業倒閉後的回收率可能遠低於往常。DoubleLine的Robert Cohen預期，部分高負債CCC級借款人無論總體經濟如何，都將需要重整，但不認為這些壓力足以顯示信用週期轉折。週五美國高收益債整體利差仍變動不大，與個別借款人的壓力形成對照。

銀行資本工具的投資人同樣要求更高補償。Bloomberg全球或有可轉債指數利差在8、9月曾低於200個基點，現已升至253個基點。BNY最新特別股發行，相較三個月前類似架構，多提供32.4個基點。Banco BPM的€4億AT1在銷售過程收窄指示性定價後，訂單由約€15億減半；Belfius新發AT1週五約為面額99%。

Atlanticomnium的Romain Miginiac特別強調，利率重設條件偏低、距可贖回日又較久的證券，有延後贖回的風險。銀行仍能取得資本，全球或有可轉債利差也仍比歷史平均低約160個基點；改變的是吸引需求所需的發行讓利。夏季定價異常緊俏之後，投資人更仔細檢視結構條款。

美國收盤後，Bloomberg報導，持有JetBlue $20億2031年到期債券及$7.42億第一順位擔保貸款的債權人，正與PJT Partners及Akin Gump合作。以忠誠會員計畫支持的債券一週跌去10美分後，約為每$1面額45美分；貸款下跌13美分，也來到45美分。證券先前已重挫，這次新增進展是聘用顧問。S&P在6月評估中預測，2026年自由現金流缺口約$10億，同時也肯定其流動性及舉債能力；原本已承壓的成本結構，仍需額外負擔債務本息。

另一起航空業執行案件，讓債權人不僅能凍結資產，還可控制現金收取。Bloomberg週五報導，倫敦法官週四委任Alvarez & Marsal接管人，追討VietJet積欠FitzWalter旗下單位逾$2.5億。接管人可改撥海外機票收入、從外國銀行帳戶取款，並扣押飛機、引擎、零件、維修準備金及交機前付款。越南境內資產不在範圍內，但VietJet未經同意，不得將受涵蓋資產移入越南或更動相關合約。這比前一週的凍結令大幅擴張了權限。

週末Braskem揭露，規模約$110億的庭外重整出現不同方案。公司申報文件表示尚未接受任何方案；知情人士則稱，各方比過去任何時候都更接近共識。兩套方案均結合增資發行與債權轉股，差異在於資金分攤及支持承諾的確定性。

公司方案要求債權人先轉股$28億，股東或第三方在$22.5億增資中承諾投入$12億，時間可能在今年。若2029年6月依特定指標判斷仍需支援，股東或第三方再投入最多$5億，另有$5億至$10億債權轉為股權。Petrobras及IG4將保留控制與經營權。

債權人也接受$22.5億增資構想，但要求股東或經核准第三方現在就為其中$18.5億提供承購保障。他們提出先轉股$18.5億，2029年6月如有需要再轉$4.5億。談判預定11月22日前結束，爭點不只減債規模，也包括新資金承諾。公司8月提出庭外債務重整申請後，各方正努力避免進一步聲請破產。

市政融資則呈現發行持續、個別交易仍受嚴格檢視的不同面貌。州及地方政府借款以歷來最快速度突破$5,000億，比去年同期多近6%，全年可望超過$6,000億。Bloomberg市政債指數10月截至週四上漲2.8%，有望創至少30年來最佳10月表現，並成為6月以來首個上漲月份。

The Villages週二為擴建籌得近$1.8億，包括3,860戶住宅。其未評級10年期債券殖利率4.7%，比基準高近1個百分點；Bloomberg高收益市政債指數最差殖利率則為5.93%。資金用於住宅開發，不是休閒設施。在整體供給增加之際，這筆融資仍顯示投資人對特定擴建案有需求。

Flyland Recovery Network擬出售八家治療中心，帶來不同的承銷風險問題。新成立的非營利機構Stepstone Health Foundation計畫發行2062年到期的$2.925億優先順位債，以及2067年到期的$2.107億次順位零息債，均無評級。Flyland將取得約$2.24億現金及該次順位債，其高階主管則至少繼續營運設施15年，收取營收總額4%的費用。至2030年，只有優先順位債持有人獲付款，這筆費用才可支付。

Columbia Threadneedle的Shannon Rinehart表示，因共同創辦人Kyle Robertson過去曾因詐欺定罪，該公司不會參與。RBC銀行家Jenn Ewing則認為，持續參與管理可讓經營誘因一致；相關業務曾產生約$4,100萬調整後EBITDA。Stepstone只會以$1,080萬購入兩處設施的不動產，其餘六處採租賃，因此不動產擔保有限。

治理疑慮也延伸至市政債發行平台。SEC對監督及顧問費揭露提出疑慮後，聖地牙哥確認，待未完成交易結束後，將退出California Statewide Communities Development Authority。監管機關正質疑可能涉及利益衝突且揭露不足的報酬安排。該機構在2025財政年度末有$240億債券流通在外，但對市府9月函件有不同解讀，仍表示相信聖地牙哥會留下。

## 後續市場焦點

週五企業活動擴張、家庭通膨預期上升之後，10月28日聯準會決策是最重要的排定觀察點。共識預期政策利率維持4%，決議於UTC 18:00公布，記者會為18:30。Bloomberg週末報導引述的交換市場定價顯示，10月升息機率低於15%。部分借款人的融資管道已受市場收緊影響，主席Kevin Warsh如何區分「現在暫停」與「之後可能緊縮」，將相當重要。

第一批美國成長數據在週一登場：9月芝加哥聯準銀行全國活動指數預測為負0.1，前值負0.04；10月達拉斯聯準銀行製造業指數預測7，前值9.8。週二還有ADP每週就業、耐久財訂單、住宅數據及世界大型企業研究會消費者信心。9月耐久財訂單預計月增0.6%，前月持平；不含運輸項目亦預計增0.6%，前值0.3%。消費者信心共識80.5，前值81.9；新屋銷售預期66萬戶，前值68.4萬戶。這些數據將延續企業調查韌性與家庭購買條件受損之間的對照。

週四第三季GDP初值預期成長3.2%，高於前值2.2%；亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow模型估值為3.5%，與即將公布的政府數據性質不同。9月核心PCE物價指數預期月增0.3%，前值0.2%；整體PCE預期增0.5%，前值0.3%。個人所得與支出均預期增0.3%，前值分別為0.2%及0.9%。這批在政策決議後一同公布的數據，將影響後續對需求韌性及通膨持續性的判斷。

美債供給將另行檢驗需求：週一標售2年期、週二5年期、週四7年期。交易商預期下週美國投資級公司債發行約$300億，與公債行事曆共同形成潛在借款需求。歐洲近60%受訪專業人士預期發行€150億至€250億。KEXIM延後發債、銀行資本工具重新定價後，借款人能否以可接受條件完成發行，尤其值得留意。

歐洲政策與財政事件密集。10月29日ECB決策，將檢驗官員在法國承受融資收緊時，是否繼續區分能源通膨與第二輪壓力。英國10月28日預算則將John Healey的財政保證，化為具體借款及支出決策。週末報導指出，預期財政緩衝至少£150億，暫時性能源紓困將針對特定對象、由提高銀行稅支應，不普遍加稅；國防及福利決策則仍部分延後。這些條件將影響預算公布前已出現的長天期英國公債需求。

日本10月30日央行決策及新展望，將檢驗公債漲勢能否承受最新CPI與官員認為政策仍低於中性的看法；當天稍早先有東京通膨數據。澳洲週三通膨公布，則更直接關係11月3日澳洲央行決策。助理總裁Sarah Hunter週日受訪表示，今年升息四次後，抑制通膨的工作尚未完成，但不預先替理事會表態。她認為，更多油價壓力正進入供應鏈，但房價下跌未帶來系統性金融壓力。Bloomberg Economics預期第三季截尾平均通膨為3.6%，與前一季相近。

截至週日的報導，巴西總統第二輪選舉仍未有結果。Datafolha最新民調顯示，Lula與Flavio Bolsonaro同為50%，市場下一步評估將取決於選舉結果，以及勝選者財政計畫的可信度。Bolsonaro陣營成員私下質疑，削減約2,000億巴西里耳、相當於GDP約1.5%的支出是否可行。投票前市場已上漲，投資人預期的財政調整與政府實際能推動的措施，仍須區分。

亞洲盤前出現了與週五收盤不同的新發展。Bloomberg週一清晨報導，那斯達克100期貨上漲0.6%，標普500期貨上漲0.4%，布蘭特原油下跌逾1%、接近$115。川普表示，與德黑蘭達成協議或美國再度發動攻擊，已接近決定時刻；美國也減少區域部分地點的外交與軍事人員，利雅德機場則於週日恢復開放。油價短線回落之際，軍事行動仍有不確定性。這些發展連同SpaceX融資狀態的爭議，構成本週新的起點，與已完成交易日殖利率及能源價格上升的行情分開看待。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries surrendered part of their sharp rally as another jump in oil restored pressure on borrowing costs, even while investors continued to question the financing of the artificial-intelligence boom. The 10-year yield rose 4.15 basis points to 4.9945%, with broadly similar increases at two and 30 years. Brent finished at $116.72 a barrel as renewed Middle East violence threatened supplies. A pause in the technology selloff reduced the immediate demand for safety without producing a broad recovery in risk appetite.

Fresh U.S. economic readings gave the Federal Reserve little reason to regard weaker consumer confidence as relief from inflation. October business surveys still showed expansion, including a manufacturing result above consensus. Michigan sentiment remained at a five-month low, but its final reading improved from the preliminary estimate while both short- and longer-term inflation expectations rose. The combination was one of strained household purchasing power alongside continued business growth, rather than a uniform deterioration in activity.

Credit remained more selective than government bonds. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened noticeably, while high-yield spreads were little changed on the day despite severe losses in individual lower-rated borrowers. SpaceX's chip financing, new details of the structures supporting AI debt and a sharp fall in Ineos Quattro bonds exposed different vulnerabilities: competition for capital, concentrated contractual support and operating earnings insufficient to ease a large refinancing burden. France's bonds recovered some ground before a rating reprieve announced just after the U.S. fixed-income close, even as new business surveys showed its economy contracting.

## Oil and Household Inflation Check the Treasury Rally

Friday's Treasury retreat was relatively even across the main maturities. The two-year yield increased 4.22 basis points to 4.6818%, the five-year rose 3.54 basis points to 4.8067%, and the 30-year advanced 4.17 basis points to 5.3221%. The 2s10s spread barely changed, narrowing 0.07 basis point to 31.27 basis points. The session therefore reversed part of the previous day's price gain without introducing a significant new curve adjustment.

Government bonds still ended the week stronger. Ten-year yields were down 7.83 basis points over the week and 30-year yields 9.88 basis points lower, compared with a 2.65-basis-point decline at two years. Over the month, however, the 10-year remained 3.15 basis points higher and the 30-year 2.21 basis points higher, while the two-year was 7.42 basis points lower. The weekly recovery at longer maturities had not removed the broader burden of high financing costs.

Both real yields and inflation compensation contributed to Friday's reversal. The 10-year TIPS yield rose 2.98 basis points to 2.6415%, accounting for most of the nominal increase, while the 10-year breakeven rose 1.17 basis points to 2.353%. Over the week, real yields had fallen 8.05 basis points while breakevens edged up 0.22 basis point. The sustained weekly support for Treasuries came through lower real yields, not a retreat in longer-run inflation compensation.

Energy was moving forcefully in the other direction. Brent gained 3.14% Friday, bringing its weekly rise to 6.24% and its monthly advance to 22.34%. WTI rose 3.82% to $103.27, up 4.29% over the week and 17.38% over the month. Bloomberg's market account linked the renewed increase to a flare-up in Middle East violence and threats to supply. A separate account of physical trading described cheaper Middle Eastern barrels while flows through Hormuz continued, showing that the futures risk premium was rising faster than the evidence of lost supply.

The equity market's stabilization was similarly incomplete. The Nasdaq 100 slipped less than 0.01%, and semiconductor shares recovered 0.44%, but the S&P 500 fell 0.52%. Chip stocks remained down 3.21% over the week and 15.05% over the month. The VIX increased 2.21% to 19.45, and the Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 101.81. Technology selling had paused; the broader market was still absorbing expensive energy and uncertainty about the cost of capital.

October's flash S&P Global purchasing managers' indexes supplied an important current counterweight to the growth concerns behind the Treasury rally. The U.S. composite eased to 57.6 from 58.4, matching the calendar forecast. Services slowed to 57.9 from 58.8, just below the 58 consensus. Manufacturing increased to 56.0 from 55.9, exceeding the 55.5 consensus. Both sectors remained above the 50 dividing line between expansion and contraction, with manufacturing marginally strengthening rather than joining the services slowdown.

Households gave a less comfortable account. The University of Michigan's final October sentiment index was 48.0, up from the preliminary 46.3 and above the 46.3 consensus, but slightly below September's 48.1. The result remained a five-month low. Interviews ran from September 22 to October 19, capturing concerns about high prices, limited hiring and elevated mortgage rates rather than only the latest trading-day headlines.

The weakness was concentrated in consumers' assessment of present circumstances. Current conditions fell to 46.7 from 50.9, while expectations improved to 48.8 from 46.3. The decline in current conditions came entirely from durable-goods buying conditions, which dropped 18% amid higher interest rates and affordability concerns and reached a record low. Nearly 70% of respondents expected interest rates to rise over the next year, the highest share in more than three years.

There was some improvement in the outlook without a recovery in the overall level of confidence. Year-ahead business conditions rose around 14% but remained 16% below October 2025. Overall sentiment was 10% below a year earlier and 15% below February, before the Iran conflict. Gains among Republicans and Democrats were offset by a third consecutive monthly decline among independents.

Inflation expectations moved higher at the same time. Consumers expected prices to rise 4.7% over the next year, against 4.6% in September, and 3.5% over the next five to 10 years, up from 3.4%. Both readings were the highest since May. Survey director Joanne Hsu warned that recent increases after five years of above-target inflation exposed a risk of expectations becoming entrenched. The survey thus paired poorer buying conditions with a firmer expected price path, a combination that complicates the policy response to weaker confidence.

Pimco economist Tiffany Wilding argued that inflation was elevated but not accelerating, leaving the Fed room for a measured approach even as it leaned against AI-supported demand. That assessment differed in emphasis from the household survey's rising expectations. Neither the continued expansion in the PMIs nor Michigan's affordability deterioration supported a simple account of collapsing activity accompanied by declining price pressure.

Demand for bonds nonetheless remained substantial beyond the daily reversal. Bloomberg Intelligence put October inflows into bond ETFs at roughly $58 billion, about 38% of all ETF flows. Fixed income had captured more than 35% for a second consecutive month, the first back-to-back stretch since early last year. BI's Athanasios Psarofagis attributed the strength to a combination of more defensive allocations and attractive income. Those monthly flows accompanied, rather than eliminated, Friday's losses: investment-grade fund LQD returned about minus 0.41%, while HYG's return was about minus 0.06%.

## AI Financing Tests Structures as Well as Borrowers

Friday brought a further rise in the cost of insuring blue-chip corporate debt. The CDX Investment-Grade Index climbed as much as 1.5 basis points to 64.4 during the day, its highest intraday level since March. In Asia, higher-rated dollar corporate spreads reached their widest since July 2025, while euro investment-grade spreads reached levels last seen in May 2025. The pressure was extending across funding markets even where technology equities had stopped falling.

SpaceX's 6.6% bonds due in 2046 widened 13 basis points to 279 basis points over Treasuries by 4 p.m. New York time, according to Trace. The deterioration accompanied negotiations over a $40 billion structure to buy Nvidia chips without adding the liabilities to SpaceX's own balance sheet. Its investment-grade status was central to the transaction, with the proposed separation of the debt intended to protect ratings while capital needs continued to grow.

Goldman Sachs was leading discussions with investors led by Apollo, according to people familiar with the talks. Apollo-backed Atlas SP was expected to manage the financing entity, Pimco was considering participation, and Goldman might retain some debt. The proposed private-placement package comprised three tranches: a subordinated portion of $25 billion-$30 billion, another of $10 billion and a third of as much as $5 billion. Earlier spread discussions had ranged from 230 basis points above benchmarks to more than 300 basis points. A subordinated yield discussed in the mid-8% range had become harder to settle as market volatility intensified.

The accounting treatment was financially consequential. SpaceX's latest earnings report disclosed that about $13 billion from an earlier xAI financing attempt had ultimately been recorded as its own debt after auditors classified the transaction as a failed sale-leaseback. That earlier entity had sought as much as $20 billion with Valor Equity Partners. The new financing effort therefore faced a practical precedent in which a structure intended to separate liabilities had not achieved the desired accounting result.

On Sunday, after the completed U.S. session, Elon Musk said on X that SpaceX had closed the $40 billion chip financing, citing its investment-grade rating and revenue from Starlink and rocket launches. People familiar with the transaction told Bloomberg that pricing discussions were still under way Sunday and the deal had not closed. Musk also argued that lenders had largely shut off funding for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers and predicted consolidation among neoclouds. His completion claim and the contrary account left the transaction's status disputed at the start of the Asian week.

New reporting on chip-backed finance showed why creditors were distinguishing corporate risk from individual transaction risk. CoreWeave's corporate junk bonds had fallen in some cases to around 80 cents on the dollar, yielding roughly 15%, while its two chip-backed leveraged loans remained near par after small declines. Investors were assigning different values to claims on the expanding company and claims supported by specific customer contracts and hardware.

The basic structure places chips in a special-purpose vehicle that borrows against customer cash flows and the equipment itself. Contract payments cover interest and amortize the borrowing, with maturities commonly aligned to an expected chip depreciation period of five to six years. Chips cost two to four times as much as the data centers housing them, according to Bloomberg's examination. At Nscale's flagship West Virginia development, the expected GPU bill was $47 billion, compared with $18 billion for the data center and equipment and $6.5 billion for the power plant.

That short hardware life creates a large and recurring financing requirement. JPMorgan analysts estimated chip spending could exceed $3 trillion through 2030, with most likely financed through debt. Vendor support is helping connect that requirement to investment-grade pools of capital. Nvidia has announced a $500 billion partnership with six major lenders and would backstop up to 25% of an opportunity under the coalition it assembled in August. Broadcom was working with Wall Street on a $60 billion financing entity to buy chips and lease them to Anthropic.

The price of credit changes sharply with the contractual support. CoreWeave's initial $2.3 billion private-credit borrowing in 2023, led by Blackstone and backed by Microsoft contracts, carried an interest rate in the mid-teens. An $8.5 billion package backed by Meta contracts in March carried borrowing costs of roughly 6%, as lenders assessed that transaction against Meta's stronger credit standing. These were separate financings with different terms and dates, illustrating the importance of the customer behind the contract rather than a general decline in CoreWeave's corporate funding cost.

Apollo and Blackstone's $35 billion Big Sky financing for Anthropic supplied another example. Broadcom agreed that, if Anthropic defaulted, chips would be re-leased or sold and it would cover any remaining shortfall. That support gave two senior tranches investment-grade ratings. The largest paid 5.75%, while the riskier $4.5 billion junior tranche paid 8.5%. The platform behind the transaction could finance 20 gigawatts of capacity, which Bank of America strategists estimated might require $235 billion of backstopped debt by mid-2029.

Those protections concentrate reliance on a small group of chipmakers and customers. Fitch's Jason Pompeii warned that vendor financing on this scale increased the potential for disappointment in AI to spread through the supply chain. Carlyle's Akhil Bansal questioned the practical balance of power if a handful of technology firms supplying credit support later demanded changes to contracts. Nuveen's Laura Parrott was holding back from large investment-grade chip deals until the market had more experience with how the structures performed during disruption. Apollo's Chris Edson, by contrast, emphasized transactions with collateral, amortization, limited residual or renewal risk, diversification and high-grade customers.

Capital raising outside debt markets also became more difficult. SK Hynix abandoned a potential $10 billion U.S. listing of Solidigm after regulatory and shareholder opposition, including concern about minority-investor dilution and ownership complexity. OpenAI reduced the valuation sought for a roughly $30 billion funding round to $1.25 trillion from an earlier $1.4 trillion figure, according to Bloomberg's account. The Solidigm withdrawal had a specific governance cause, while OpenAI's revised ambition directly changed its proposed equity terms.

In yen credit, Export-Import Bank of Korea postponed a sale it had been preparing to price as early as October 23. The lender said volatility prevented it from achieving its desired size at planned pricing and that it had no urgent funding need. It had sounded out demand for three-, five- and seven-year maturities. Competition for buyers was substantial: more than ¥2.5 trillion of corporate bonds had priced during October through Friday, a record for the month, including ¥400 billion from Rakuten and ¥281 billion from Mizuho Bank. NTT Finance raised ¥70 billion rather than the roughly ¥100 billion planned, while Mitsui Fudosan had shelved a sale.

## France Wins a Rating Reprieve as Activity Contracts

French bonds recovered Friday, with the 10-year premium over Germany narrowing 7 basis points, the most since October 6. The gap remained around 1.7 percentage points and was up 29 basis points over the week, the second-largest weekly increase in data going back to 1990. The day's improvement reduced the immediate pressure without undoing the accumulated repricing of French fiscal risk.

The new economic evidence was weaker than expected. France's October S&P Global composite PMI fell to 48.4 from 51.1, against a forecast of 50.3. Both manufacturing and services dropped below 50. Private-sector sales declined at their fastest pace since May, with reduced purchasing and investment accompanying tighter financing and political pressure, according to S&P Global economist Joe Hayes. Expectations for activity over the next year fell to a six-and-a-half-year low.

That contraction gave a concrete growth dimension to the budget difficulty. Moody's, in a decision reported just after 5 p.m. New York time, maintained France at Aa3 with a negative outlook rather than delivering the downgrade investors had anticipated. It said slower growth and a higher deficit had raised the debt burden beyond previous expectations, while yields had risen faster than forecast and protests could constrain consolidation. France retained its last major double-A rating, one notch above S&P and Fitch.

Moody's assumed that a deficit-reducing 2027 budget would eventually be adopted, possibly by decree. The deficit was projected at 5.4% of GDP this year, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's proposed spending restraint and higher tax revenue aimed for 5% next year. With no parliamentary majority, the means of delivering that reduction remained uncertain. On Friday the National Assembly rejected the revenue portion of the social-security budget, sending the original draft to the Senate, with debate on the main budget due to resume the following week.

The ECB was confronting the distinction between a common energy shock and country-specific fiscal pressure. Its consumer survey showed one-year inflation expectations rising to 3.1% in September from 3% in August, while three-year expectations held at 2.9% and five-year expectations at 2.5%. The increase was concentrated at the shorter horizon rather than spread across all three measures.

A new Bloomberg economist survey also highlighted a gap between policy forecasts and market pricing. An overwhelming majority expected one final quarter-point increase in December to a 2.75% deposit rate, followed by a hold until May 2028. Traders expected three more increases over the next year. Rabobank's Bas van Geffen cited the absence of broader wage- and price-setting effects from energy as a reason to wait; International School of Management lecturer Dennis Shen argued that a prolonged headline overshoot increased medium-term risks to expectations and wages.

Economists saw a high threshold for direct ECB support of sovereign bonds. About 70% ruled out intervention in any form and around 90% ruled out the Transmission Protection Instrument. Bank J Safra Sarasin's Karsten Junius said stronger global demand for capital and deteriorating public finances made a TPI operation difficult to justify. Some respondents saw more scope for softer rate guidance or an end to quantitative tightening. Those possibilities differed substantially from purchases aimed at suppressing France's borrowing premium.

Leadership negotiations were becoming entangled with that challenge. Euro-area ministers extended the application deadline for Isabel Schnabel's Executive Board seat to November 27 from October 28, increasing the possibility of a package covering her successor, the presidency and Philip Lane's position. In the economist survey, 12 respondents chose Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the likely next president and nine chose Klaas Knot. Only a third expected Christine Lagarde to finish her term in October 2027, compared with almost 60% in the previous poll.

Weekend reporting described governments placing greater weight on crisis-management credibility as they assessed the candidates. Former ECB chief economist Peter Praet stressed intervention conditions and central-bank independence, while de Cos had warned in a speech this month that even well-designed operations could be interpreted through a fiscal lens when public financing needs were large. Knot's paper this month defended emergency instruments where fragmentation threatened monetary-policy transmission. The debate was about the conditions for action as much as the willingness to act.

Britain presented a different investor response to fiscal risk. Rathbones bought 10-year gilts and sold debt due in two to five years across its £9.6 billion multi-asset portfolio, moving longer-duration exposure from underweight to neutral. David Coombs cited more disciplined budget messaging and real yields near 2%, but retained doubts about spending restraint. Royal London managers Craig Inches and Ben Nicholl had separately moved overweight 30-year gilts, pointing to fiscal discipline, reduced long-end issuance and changes to the Bank of England's quantitative-tightening program.

Royal London remained wary of short gilts because inflation could force the BOE to deliver further increases, with markets pricing more than 100 basis points over the next year. The preference for longer maturities rested on supply and fiscal developments, not confidence that the near-term inflation challenge had disappeared. Bloomberg's Friday market account put the 10-year gilt yield up 3 basis points at 5.36%, alongside a 1-basis-point rise in Germany's to 3.35%.

## Japan's Bond Rally Meets Firmer Inflation and Policy Signals

Japanese government bonds rallied strongly despite fresh inflation evidence supporting further BOJ tightening. The 10-year yield fell 12.5 basis points to 2.755% during Friday trading, and the five-year dropped as much as 10.5 basis points to 2.185%. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura said the decline at short and intermediate maturities suggested investors were allowing for a delay in hikes if the technology slump and European debt stress became a lasting financial shock.

September consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 2.1% from a year earlier, matching the median forecast and exceeding the BOJ's target for the first time this year. The measure excluding fresh food and energy increased 2.4%, while headline CPI rose 2.1%. Services inflation accelerated to 1.5%, the fastest since March. Food prices excluding fresh items rose 2.9% even as rice fell 20.6%, the largest decline in data extending back to 1971.

The breadth of the price detail mattered alongside energy. Hotel, water and food costs led the gains, while the gasoline tax cut continued to restrain consumer energy bills. Teikoku Databank said major food and beverage companies planned increases on 3,153 items in October, a second consecutive month above 3,000 for the first time since July 2023. Businesses' willingness to pass on costs gave the BOJ a domestic pricing signal even as global risk aversion pulled yields lower.

People familiar with the BOJ's thinking told Bloomberg that officials viewed underlying inflation as broadly consistent with 2% and the policy rate as still some distance below neutral. They saw scope to sustain the recent roughly quarterly pace of increases if the economy and prices evolved as expected, while assessing cumulative effects and risks without a predetermined path. They felt no urgency to act immediately after September's increase. That account placed a policy counterweight beside the market's defensive rally.

China's borrowing costs were moving lower for different reasons. The finance ministry sold 15.5 billion yuan of offshore sovereign bonds Friday, setting record-low auction yields at two, five and 10 years of 1.24%, 1.38% and 1.67%. Three-year notes yielded 1.28%, the lowest since 2011. The overall bid-to-cover ratio fell to 3.43, its lowest since May 2025. Record-low yields thus came with a weaker aggregate bidding ratio, rather than uniformly stronger demand measures.

Onshore, the 30-year auction's bid-to-cover ratio rose to a record in data going back to 2007, after allowing for a smaller offering. The PBOC added cash on a net basis for a third day, and the overnight repo rate was near a multi-month low at 1.27%. These funding conditions accompanied a rally in which the onshore 10-year yield had fallen around 5 basis points during October.

Friday's fiscal figures showed why government support had not yet translated into stronger spending. Bloomberg calculations based on Ministry of Finance data put September broad expenditure down 3.7% from a year earlier, a seventh monthly decline, though less severe than August's 6.7% fall. Revenue declined 3.5%, and the monthly deficit narrowed 3.8%. Broad spending exceeded income by 7.57 trillion yuan over the first nine months.

Local governments had issued 3.56 trillion yuan of new special bonds, 81% of the annual budget plan, yet broad expenditure had reached only 65% of its full-year target, against 67% a year earlier. Land-sale revenue fell 27.9% in the first nine months, pulling land-related spending down 18.5%. The ministry identified an intention to accelerate allocation of next year's special-bond quota so sales could begin in January. The financing pipeline and actual deployment were moving at different speeds.

Elsewhere, monetary decisions remained highly country-specific. Russia held its key rate at 14%, with Governor Elvira Nabiullina saying the board had discussed only a hold in detail. Slower restoration of industrial capacity damaged by Ukrainian attacks required moderately tight policy for longer than previously expected. The central bank projected year-end inflation of 7.1%-7.6%, a 12.5%-13.5% average policy rate next year and 2026 growth of 0.5%-1%, revised from 0%-1%. Nabiullina said major companies needing debt restructurings mostly faced temporary difficulties and saw no threat to financial stability.

Kazakhstan cut 50 basis points to 15.75%, its fourth consecutive reduction, after inflation slowed to 9.3% in September. Three surveyed economists expected that size of move and four expected 25 basis points. The bank said another change this year was unlikely, citing elevated price pressure, inflationary risks and the prospect that regulated-tariff base effects would lift inflation again. Its easing decision came with an explicit limit on the near-term continuation of cuts.

India's Sanjay Malhotra said Friday that interest rates could be used for financial stability in some circumstances, though price stability remained their primary purpose. He reiterated that the RBI targeted orderly currency trading rather than a rupee level. The currency ended at 94.94 per dollar after approaching 97 earlier in the month. The RBI's bulletin warned of broadening food and fuel inflation and possible second-round effects, while Malhotra noted that September's 5.54% inflation remained within the 2%-6% tolerance band around its 4% target.

Indonesia's credit repricing showed how an equity-market governance issue could extend into debt. Its corporate premium over regional peers had risen 28 basis points to 67 basis points, the widest since 2020, after MSCI's reclassification warning. Bank Mandiri's AT1 had fallen 3 points since the October 15 announcement to around 95 cents, against a 0.8-point decline for Asian high yield overall; Bank Negara Indonesia's comparable security was near 94 after six consecutive declines. Senior debt at both remained around 99 cents. Nomura's Nicholas Yap cited strong capital and funding as buffers at the large banks, while expecting subordinated valuations to remain under pressure until the index decision or domestic sentiment became clearer.

## Earnings and Creditor Terms Drive Distressed Debt

Ineos Quattro's Friday earnings update produced one of the clearest issuer-specific shocks. Q3 EBITDA fell to €162 million from €177 million a year earlier and €407 million in Q2, when disruption of Asian imports had temporarily supported pricing. Its March 2029 bonds dropped 9 cents on the euro, heading for their largest daily fall since issuance in November 2023. Default insurance rose to 31 points upfront from 25.6 points, according to ICE Data Services.

The company blamed the return of low-cost Asian imports and persistently high energy costs, especially in Europe. Inovyn's EBITDA fell to €13 million from €64 million a year earlier as import-related pricing support largely disappeared and electricity and gas costs rose. Chinese oversupply also squeezed polymer margins, while the U.S. remained a stronger market. Bloomberg Intelligence's Timothy Riminton highlighted about €4 billion of maturities in 2029. The new earnings decline reduced the operating cushion ahead of that refinancing burden.

Broader research showed deeper distress in the lower-rated tail. JPMorgan said September loan volume below 60 cents was the highest since March 2020, while the amount at or below 80 cents had increased almost 90% in 12 months. The gap between CCC and BB spreads was the widest since the pandemic. Cable and satellite borrowers were among the weakest performers, facing both high financing costs and competition from new distribution technologies.

The distinction between concentrated losses and a broad credit downturn remained contested. CPP Investments' David Colla warned that recoveries on failed companies could be much lower than usual. DoubleLine's Robert Cohen expected some heavily indebted CCC borrowers to restructure regardless of the macroeconomic outcome, but did not regard their stress as evidence of a credit cycle. These assessments sat alongside Friday's little-changed broad U.S. high-yield spreads, rather than a uniform same-day deterioration across the market.

Bank capital investors were also demanding more compensation. Bloomberg's global contingent-convertible index spread had risen to 253 basis points after dipping below 200 in August and September. BNY's latest preferred issue offered 32.4 basis points more than a similar structure three months earlier. Orders for Banco BPM's €400 million AT1 fell by half from about €1.5 billion as marketing tightened indicative pricing, while Belfius' newly issued AT1 was around 99 cents on the euro Friday.

Atlanticomnium's Romain Miginiac emphasized extension risk in securities with low reset terms and distant calls. Banks still had access to capital, and global contingent-convertible spreads remained around 160 basis points below their historical average. The change was in the concessions needed to secure demand, with structural terms receiving greater scrutiny after the summer's exceptionally tight pricing.

After the U.S. close, Bloomberg reported that JetBlue creditors holding $2 billion of 2031 bonds and a $742 million first-lien loan were working with PJT Partners and Akin Gump. The loyalty-backed bonds were around 45 cents after losing 10 cents over the week, and the loan had fallen 13 cents to 45. The adviser appointments were the new development following the earlier collapse in its securities. S&P's June assessment projected a roughly $1 billion free-cash-flow deficit for 2026, while recognizing liquidity and borrowing capacity; debt service remained an additional burden on an already pressured cost structure.

A separate aviation enforcement action gave creditors control over cash collection rather than simply freezing assets. A London judge appointed Alvarez & Marsal receivers Thursday to recover more than $250 million owed by VietJet to a FitzWalter unit, Bloomberg reported Friday. The receivers can redirect overseas ticket receipts, take money from foreign bank accounts and seize aircraft, engines, spare parts, maintenance reserves and pre-delivery payments. Vietnamese assets are excluded, but VietJet is barred from moving covered assets into Vietnam or changing relevant contracts without consent. The order materially expanded on the previous week's freezing injunction.

Over the weekend, Braskem disclosed competing proposals for its roughly $11 billion out-of-court restructuring. Its filing said no proposal had been accepted, while people familiar with talks described the sides as closer than at any previous point. Both approaches combine a follow-on equity offering and a creditor debt-to-equity conversion, but differ over the division and certainty of support.

Under the company's proposal, creditors would convert $2.8 billion and shareholders or third parties would commit $1.2 billion within a $2.25 billion offering, probably this year. If specified metrics required more support in June 2029, shareholders or third parties would contribute up to $500 million more and $500 million-$1 billion of creditor debt would convert into equity. Petrobras and IG4 would retain control and management.

Creditors also accepted the idea of a $2.25 billion offering but wanted $1.85 billion backstopped now by shareholders or approved third parties. They proposed an initial $1.85 billion debt conversion and another $450 million in June 2029 if needed. The negotiations, due to conclude by November 22, concern the commitment of fresh capital as well as the size of the debt reduction. The parties were trying to avert a bankruptcy filing after the August extrajudicial-recovery application.

Municipal finance offered a contrasting picture of continuing issuance and transaction-level scrutiny. State and local borrowing passed $500 billion at a record pace, almost 6% above the same point last year and on course to exceed $600 billion for the year. The Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index had gained 2.8% in October through Thursday, on track for its strongest October in at least 30 years and its first positive month since June.

The Villages raised almost $180 million Tuesday for expansion, including 3,860 residential units. Its unrated 10-year bonds yielded 4.7%, nearly 1 percentage point above their benchmark, compared with a 5.93% yield-to-worst on the Bloomberg high-yield municipal index. Proceeds are for residential development rather than recreational facilities. The financing demonstrated demand for a specific expansion project even amid rising aggregate supply.

Flyland Recovery Network's proposed sale of eight treatment centers raised a different underwriting question. New nonprofit Stepstone Health Foundation planned $292.5 million of senior debt due in 2062 and $210.7 million of subordinated zero-coupon debt due in 2067, with no ratings. Flyland would receive about $224 million in cash and the junior debt, while its executives would operate the facilities for at least 15 years for a fee of 4% of gross revenue. Through 2030, that fee would be payable only if senior bondholders were paid.

Columbia Threadneedle's Shannon Rinehart said the firm would not participate because of co-founder Kyle Robertson's past fraud conviction. RBC banker Jenn Ewing argued that the continuing management role aligned incentives with operations that had generated about $41 million of adjusted EBITDA. Stepstone would buy the real estate at only two facilities for $10.8 million and lease the other six, limiting real-estate collateral. The proposed transaction therefore combined an explicit management objection, a conditional fee protection and limited property security.

Governance concerns extended to municipal issuance platforms. San Diego confirmed plans to leave the California Statewide Communities Development Authority once pending transactions were complete after SEC concerns about oversight and consultant fee disclosure. The authority, with $24 billion of bonds outstanding at fiscal 2025's end, interpreted the city's September letter differently and said it believed San Diego was remaining. The city's confirmation preserved a live disagreement over membership as regulators questioned potentially conflicted and insufficiently disclosed compensation arrangements.

## Forward Market Significance

The October 28 Fed decision is the central scheduled test after Friday's combination of expanding business activity and rising household inflation expectations. Consensus expects the policy rate to remain at 4%, with the announcement at 18:00 UTC and the press conference at 18:30 UTC. Swaps cited in Bloomberg's weekend account put the chance of an October increase below 15%. Chair Kevin Warsh's handling of the difference between a pause now and possible tightening later will matter when market-driven restraint is already evident in some borrowers' access to capital.

The first U.S. growth checks arrive Monday: September's Chicago Fed National Activity Index, forecast at minus 0.1 after minus 0.04, and October Dallas Fed manufacturing, forecast at 7 after 9.8. Tuesday adds weekly ADP employment, durable-goods orders, housing figures and Conference Board confidence. Durable orders are expected to rise 0.6% in September after no change, with the ex-transportation measure also expected up 0.6% after 0.3%. Consumer confidence consensus is 80.5 after 81.9, and new-home sales are expected at 660,000 after 684,000. These releases will extend the comparison between resilient business surveys and impaired household buying conditions.

Thursday's initial Q3 GDP estimate is expected to show 3.2% growth after 2.2%, while the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model stood at 3.5%. The model estimate remains distinct from the forthcoming government result. September core PCE is expected to rise 0.3% on the month after 0.2%, with headline PCE expected up 0.5% after 0.3%. Personal income and spending are each expected to increase 0.3%, against previous gains of 0.2% and 0.9%. Released together after the policy decision, the figures will shape the subsequent judgment about demand resilience and inflation persistence.

Treasury supply provides separate demand tests, with two-year notes scheduled Monday, five-year notes Tuesday and seven-year notes Thursday. Dealer expectations for roughly $30 billion of U.S. investment-grade corporate issuance next week place additional prospective borrowing beside the sovereign calendar. In Europe, nearly 60% of professionals surveyed expected €15 billion-€25 billion of issuance. The ability to complete sales at acceptable terms remains especially relevant after KEXIM's postponement and the repricing of bank capital.

Europe's policy and fiscal events are closely spaced. The ECB decision on October 29 will test whether officials sustain the distinction between energy inflation and second-round pressure while France absorbs tighter financing. Britain's October 28 budget will turn John Healey's fiscal assurances into borrowing and spending decisions. Weekend reporting indicated an expected fiscal buffer of at least £15 billion, targeted temporary energy relief financed by higher bank taxes and no broad tax increase; defense and welfare decisions remained partly deferred. Those terms matter to the demand for long gilts that has developed ahead of the announcement.

Japan's October 30 BOJ decision and new outlook will test the durability of its bond rally against the fresh CPI evidence and officials' view that policy remains below neutral. Tokyo inflation is due earlier that day. Australia's Wednesday inflation release is more immediately tied to the November 3 RBA decision. In a Sunday interview, Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said the bank was not yet finished containing inflation after four increases this year, while declining to pre-empt the board. She saw more oil-related pressure entering supply chains but no systemic financial stress from falling house prices. Bloomberg Economics expected Q3 trimmed-mean inflation of 3.6%, similar to the preceding quarter.

Brazil's presidential runoff remained unresolved in the available Sunday reporting. The latest Datafolha poll had Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro tied at 50%, leaving the next market assessment dependent on the result and the credibility of the winner's fiscal program. Bolsonaro campaign members had privately questioned whether cutting roughly 200 billion reais, about 1.5% of GDP, was realistic. The distinction between investors' expectations of adjustment and the measures a government could deliver remains consequential after the rally into the vote.

The Asian pre-market opened with developments distinct from Friday's close. In Bloomberg's early Monday account, Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.6%, S&P 500 futures gained 0.4%, and Brent fell more than 1% toward $115. Trump said it was nearing decision time on a deal with Tehran or renewed U.S. attacks, while the U.S. reduced diplomatic and military staffing in parts of the region and Riyadh airport reopened Sunday. The immediate oil retreat accompanied continued uncertainty over military action. It introduces a new starting point for the week, alongside the disputed status of SpaceX's financing, rather than changing the completed session's rise in yields and energy prices.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries surrendered part of Thursday's rally as renewed Middle East violence raised oil supply concerns and technology selling paused. The 10-year yield rose 4.15 basis points to 4.9945%, with similar increases at two and 30 years and little change in the curve. Higher real yields accounted for 2.98 basis points of the rise and inflation compensation for 1.17 basis points. Ten-year yields nevertheless finished the week 7.83 basis points lower, driven by lower real yields rather than falling inflation compensation. Brent rose 3.14% to $116.72, although continued flows through Hormuz distinguished supply fears from evidence of lost barrels.

U.S. business surveys still showed expansion: manufacturing beat expectations even as services slowed. Michigan sentiment remained at a five-month low, with durable-goods buying conditions at a record low, while year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% and longer-term expectations to 3.5%. Weak household purchasing power was therefore not accompanied by easing expected price pressure.

U.S. investment-grade spreads widened noticeably, while broad high-yield spreads were little changed despite sharp issuer losses. SpaceX's proposed $40 billion chip financing and the contractual support behind AI borrowing drew scrutiny; Ineos Quattro's earnings decline weakened its cushion ahead of substantial 2029 maturities. French bonds recovered some ground before Moody's maintained Aa3 with a negative outlook just after the U.S. fixed-income close, despite contracting activity and unresolved budget delivery. The October 28 Fed decision is the next central test of resilient business demand against persistent inflation pressure.
